items.q: A cylinder of diameter 300 mm is developed. Find the length of the development in mm.
items.s: Development length = pi d = pi x 300 = 942.5 mm.

items.q: An ellipse has semi major axis 60 mm and semi minor axis 60 mm. Find the distance from the centre to each focus in mm.
items.s: Focal distance = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(60^2 - 60^2) = 0 mm.

items.q: A hatched section is 200 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 6 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 200/6 + 1 = 33 + 1 = 34.

items.q: A line 60 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:100. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 60 x 100 = 6000 mm = 6 m.

items.q: A distance of 80 mm on paper represents 20.0 m on site. Find the scale of the drawing as 1:n, giving n.
items.s: n = real mm / drawn mm = 20000.0/80 = 250.

items.q: A detail drawn at 1:100 appears again on a layout at 1:500. By what factor is the layout drawing smaller than the detail?
items.s: The same real length is drawn 500/100 times smaller, so the factor is 500/100 = 5.

items.q: Find the area of a A2 drawing sheet in cm2, taking its trimmed size as 594 mm by 420 mm.
A drawing sheet measures 420 mm by 297 mm. Find the length of its diagonal in mm.
items.s: Diagonal = sqrt(420^2 + 297^2) = 514.4 mm.

items.q: An edge of true length 60 mm is to be drawn in isometric. Using the isometric scale, find its drawn length in mm.
items.s: Isometric length = 0.816 x true = 0.816 x 60 = 48.96 mm.

items.q: A line measures 163 mm on an isometric drawing. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: True length = isometric/0.816 = 163/0.816 = 199.8 mm.

items.q: A pipeline runs 3000 mm in plan and rises 3000 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(3000^2 + 3000^2) = 4243 mm.

items.q: A straight line rises 2000 mm over a horizontal distance of 5000 mm. Find its angle of inclination to the horizontal in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(2000/5000) = 21.8 degrees.

items.q: A face 3000 mm long is inclined at 30 degrees to the plane of projection. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: Fore-shortened length = true x cos(angle), so true = 3000/cos(30) = 3464 mm.

items.q: Two lines forming a right triangle have lengths 4000 mm and 4000 mm at the right angle. Find the angle opposite the 4000 mm side, in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(4000/4000) = 45 degrees.

items.q: Find the area of the lateral surface development of a cylinder of diameter 400 mm and height 500 mm, in mm2.
A cone of base radius 75 mm has a slant height of 250 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 75/250 = 108 degrees.

items.q: A cone has base radius 80 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find its slant height in mm.
items.s: Slant height = sqrt(80^2 + 200^2) = 215.4 mm.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 150 mm and sector angle 120.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.3333 x 2 x pi x 150 = 314.2 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2.

items.q: A rectangular box 1000 mm by 500 mm by 400 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(1000 + 500) = 3000 mm; area = 3000 x 400 = 1200000 mm2.

items.q: Find the eccentricity of an ellipse whose semi axes are 75 mm and 60 mm.
items.s: c = sqrt(75^2 - 60^2) = 45.0; eccentricity = c/a = 0.6.

items.q: Calculate each interior angle of a regular polygon of 7 sides, in degrees.
items.s: Each interior angle = (n - 2) x 180/n = (7 - 2) x 180/7 = 128.6 degrees.

items.q: A plot of area 120.0 m2 is drawn at 1:200. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 120.0 m2 = 120000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 120000000.0/200^2 = 3000 mm2.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 68 degrees and 72 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 68 - 72 = 40 degrees.

items.q: A development sector has radius 100 mm and angle 135 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A rectangular beam 200 mm wide and 175 mm deep is cut across. Find the area of the hatched section face in mm2.
items.s: Section area = 200 x 175 = 35000 mm2.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 150 mm, top radius 100 mm and vertical height 240 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A cube of edge 40 mm is drawn in isometric. Find the length used for each edge on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Each edge is drawn at 0.816 x true = 0.816 x 40 = 32.64 mm.

items.q: A wall 30.0 m long is drawn at a scale of 1:100. Calculate its length on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Length on paper = actual in mm / scale = 30000.0/100 = 300 mm.

items.q: A cylinder of diameter 500 mm is developed. Find the length of the development in mm.
items.s: Development length = pi d = pi x 500 = 1571 mm.

items.q: An ellipse has semi major axis 90 mm and semi minor axis 40 mm. Find the distance from the centre to each focus in mm.
items.s: Focal distance = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(90^2 - 40^2) = 80.62 mm.

items.q: A hatched section is 180 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 5 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 180/5 + 1 = 36 + 1 = 37.

items.q: A line 75 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:200. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 75 x 200 = 15000 mm = 15 m.

items.q: A distance of 50 mm on paper represents 20.0 m on site. Find the scale of the drawing as 1:n, giving n.
items.s: n = real mm / drawn mm = 20000.0/50 = 400.

items.q: A detail drawn at 1:50 appears again on a layout at 1:500. By what factor is the layout drawing smaller than the detail?
items.s: The same real length is drawn 500/50 times smaller, so the factor is 500/50 = 10.

items.q: A drawing sheet measures 420 mm by 420 mm. Find the length of its diagonal in mm.
items.s: Diagonal = sqrt(420^2 + 420^2) = 594 mm.

items.q: A line measures 98 mm on an isometric drawing. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: True length = isometric/0.816 = 98/0.816 = 120.1 mm.

items.q: A pipeline runs 4000 mm in plan and rises 2000 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(4000^2 + 2000^2) = 4472 mm.

items.q: A straight line rises 1000 mm over a horizontal distance of 4000 mm. Find its angle of inclination to the horizontal in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(1000/4000) = 14.04 degrees.

items.q: A face 4000 mm long is inclined at 45 degrees to the plane of projection. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: Fore-shortened length = true x cos(angle), so true = 4000/cos(45) = 5657 mm.

items.q: Two lines forming a right triangle have lengths 5000 mm and 4000 mm at the right angle. Find the angle opposite the 4000 mm side, in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(4000/5000) = 38.66 degrees.

items.q: Find the area of the lateral surface development of a cylinder of diameter 300 mm and height 300 mm, in mm2.
items.s: Area = pi d h = pi x 300 x 300 = 282743 mm2.

items.q: A cone of base radius 40 mm has a slant height of 250 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 40/250 = 57.6 degrees.

items.q: A cone has base radius 60 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find its slant height in mm.
items.s: Slant height = sqrt(60^2 + 200^2) = 208.8 mm.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 180 mm and sector angle 120.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.3333 x 2 x pi x 180 = 377 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2.

items.q: A rectangular box 800 mm by 400 mm by 500 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(800 + 400) = 2400 mm; area = 2400 x 500 = 1200000 mm2.

items.q: Find the eccentricity of an ellipse whose semi axes are 60 mm and 40 mm.
Calculate each interior angle of a regular polygon of 8 sides, in degrees.
items.s: Each interior angle = (n - 2) x 180/n = (8 - 2) x 180/8 = 135 degrees.

items.q: A plot of area 96.0 m2 is drawn at 1:100. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 96.0 m2 = 96000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 96000000.0/100^2 = 9600 mm2.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 42 degrees and 61 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 42 - 61 = 77 degrees.

items.q: A development sector has radius 80 mm and angle 135 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A rectangular beam 200 mm wide and 200 mm deep is cut across. Find the area of the hatched section face in mm2.
items.s: Section area = 200 x 200 = 40000 mm2.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 180 mm, top radius 100 mm and vertical height 150 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A cube of edge 50 mm is drawn in isometric. Find the length used for each edge on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Each edge is drawn at 0.816 x true = 0.816 x 50 = 40.8 mm.

items.q: A wall 15.0 m long is drawn at a scale of 1:50. Calculate its length on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Length on paper = actual in mm / scale = 15000.0/50 = 300 mm.

items.q: A cylinder of diameter 600 mm is developed. Find the length of the development in mm.
items.s: Development length = pi d = pi x 600 = 1885 mm.

items.q: An ellipse has semi major axis 60 mm and semi minor axis 40 mm. Find the distance from the centre to each focus in mm.
items.s: Focal distance = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(60^2 - 40^2) = 44.72 mm.

items.q: A hatched section is 180 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 8 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 180/8 + 1 = 22 + 1 = 23.

items.q: A line 120 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:100. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 120 x 100 = 12000 mm = 12 m.

items.q: A distance of 40 mm on paper represents 20.0 m on site. Find the scale of the drawing as 1:n, giving n.
items.s: n = real mm / drawn mm = 20000.0/40 = 500.

items.q: Find the area of a A4 drawing sheet in cm2, taking its trimmed size as 297 mm by 210 mm.
Normal may be defined as
o: the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
a pictorial view in which the front face is drawn true and the depth is drawn at an angle
the written instruction on a drawing that a dimension cannot express
the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground
items.s: Normal: the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact. The other options describe Note, Setting out, Oblique projection.

items.q: Which term is described by “the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth”?
o: Projection line
First angle projection
Plan
End elevation
items.s: End elevation is the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth.

items.q: Which term is described by “the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane”?
o: Half section
Mean line
True shape of section
Section plane
items.s: True shape of section is the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Unidirectional dimensioning.
o: the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth
the distance from the apex of a cone to a point on the rim of its base
the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
items.s: Unidirectional dimensioning: the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom. The other options describe Drawing sheet size, Slant height, End elevation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Border line?
o: a written level at a stated point on a plan
the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet
the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane
the imaginary plane along which an object is cut for a sectional view
items.s: Border line: the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet. The other options describe Section plane, Spot level, True shape of section.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Detail drawing.
o: the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names
an oblique view in which the depth is drawn at half its true scale
the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
items.s: Detail drawing: a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built. The other options describe Line weight, Cabinet projection, Leader line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Drawing sheet size.
o: the thin line between two arrowheads that carries the value of a measurement
the panel of a drawing sheet that records the project, drawing number, scale and date
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet
items.s: Drawing sheet size: the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared. The other options describe Dimension line, Border line, Title block.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Principal plane?
o: the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected
the shortest diameter of an ellipse, perpendicular to the major axis
the reduced scale used on isometric drawings so that projected lengths match the true view
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
items.s: Principal plane: the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected. The other options describe Isometric scale, Minor axis, Drawing sheet size.

items.q: Which term is described by “the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight”?
o: Projection line
Principal view
Principal plane
Front elevation
items.s: Front elevation is the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Centre line?
o: the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature
the line that shows a part of a long object has been left out to save space
the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected
items.s: Centre line: the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature. The other options describe Tangent, Principal plane, Break line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Scale?
o: any drawing that shows an object as it appears in three dimensions
the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object
the shortest diameter of an ellipse, perpendicular to the major axis
items.s: Scale: the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object. The other options describe Inclination, Minor axis, Pictorial drawing.

items.q: Which term is described by “the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made”?
o: Arrowhead
Dimensioning
Lettering
Unidirectional dimensioning
items.s: Dimensioning is the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made.

items.q: All of the following belong to Orthographic projection EXCEPT
o: Third angle projection
Longitudinal section
Orthographic projection
First angle projection
items.s: Every other option belongs to Orthographic projection. “Longitudinal section” belongs to Civil drawing practice, not Orthographic projection.

items.q: Chain dimensioning may be defined as
o: the arrangement in which the plane lies between observer and object, so views land on the near side
a written level at a stated point on a plan
the thin evenly spaced line drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a section
the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row
items.s: Chain dimensioning: the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row. The other options describe Spot level, Third angle projection, Hatching line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cabinet projection?
o: an oblique view in which the depth is drawn at half its true scale
the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job
the thin evenly spaced line drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a section
the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total
items.s: Cabinet projection: an oblique view in which the depth is drawn at half its true scale. The other options describe Hatching line, Ellipse, Schedule of materials.

items.q: Revolved section may be defined as
o: a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself
the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind
the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
the fixed straight line from which distances define a conic curve
items.s: Revolved section: a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself. The other options describe Line weight, Directrix, Block plan.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Tee square?
o: an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale
the line that shows a part of a long object has been left out to save space
an oblique view in which the depth is drawn at half its true scale
the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines
items.s: Tee square: the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines. The other options describe Cabinet projection, Break line, Cavalier projection.

items.q: The statement “the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation” describes which of the following?
o: Revolved section
Half section
Mean line
Sectional view
items.s: Mean line is the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation.

items.q: The statement “the arrangement in which the plane lies between observer and object, so views land on the near side” describes which of the following?
o: Principal plane
Third angle projection
Orthographic projection
Plan
items.s: Third angle projection is the arrangement in which the plane lies between observer and object, so views land on the near side.

items.q: Which term is described by “the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation”?
o: Revolved section
True shape of section
Mean line
Half section
items.s: Mean line is the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind”?
o: Line weight
Centre line
Break line
Hatching line
items.s: Line weight is the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind.

items.q: Which term is described by “the curve traced when the difference of the distances from two fixed points stays constant”?
o: Minor axis
Hyperbola
Focus
Major axis
items.s: Hyperbola is the curve traced when the difference of the distances from two fixed points stays constant.

items.q: Detail drawing may be defined as
o: the heavy line with arrows that shows where a section is taken
the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
items.s: Detail drawing: a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built. The other options describe First angle projection, Cutting plane line, Eccentricity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Reducing scale?
o: the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight
the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
a scale in which the drawing is smaller than the object it represents
the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made
items.s: Reducing scale: a scale in which the drawing is smaller than the object it represents. The other options describe Tangent, Dimensioning, Front elevation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Cavalier projection.
o: an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale
the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground
the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines
the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
items.s: Cavalier projection: an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale. The other options describe Tee square, Setting out, Eccentricity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Oblique projection?
o: the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object
the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet
a pictorial view in which the front face is drawn true and the depth is drawn at an angle
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
items.s: Oblique projection: a pictorial view in which the front face is drawn true and the depth is drawn at an angle. The other options describe Scale, Normal, Border line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Major axis.
o: the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees
the longest diameter of an ellipse, passing through both foci
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
items.s: Major axis: the longest diameter of an ellipse, passing through both foci. The other options describe Block plan, Isometric projection, Projection line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Longitudinal section?
o: a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom
the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total
the curve traced when the difference of the distances from two fixed points stays constant
items.s: Longitudinal section: a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length. The other options describe Ellipse, Hyperbola, Unidirectional dimensioning.

items.q: The statement “the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane” describes which of the following?
o: Development
Inclination
True length
Lateral surface
items.s: Inclination is the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane.

items.q: The statement “the table listing each reinforcement bar with its size, shape, length and number” describes which of the following?
o: Detail drawing
Spot level
Contour line
Bar bending schedule
items.s: Bar bending schedule is the table listing each reinforcement bar with its size, shape, length and number.

items.q: Which term is described by “the longest diameter of an ellipse, passing through both foci”?
o: Minor axis
Directrix
Major axis
Eccentricity
items.s: Major axis is the longest diameter of an ellipse, passing through both foci.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Extension line?
o: the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself
a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees
the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
items.s: Extension line: the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line. The other options describe Isometric projection, Development, Revolved section.

items.q: End elevation may be defined as
o: the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total
a drawing showing the cut profile of a road, drain or embankment across its width
one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth
items.s: End elevation: the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth. The other options describe Ellipse, Cross section, Principal view.

items.q: Which term is described by “the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row”?
o: Dimensioning
Aligned dimensioning
Lettering
Chain dimensioning
items.s: Chain dimensioning is the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Orthographic projection?
o: the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles
the fixed straight line from which distances define a conic curve
items.s: Orthographic projection: the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles. The other options describe Normal, Directrix, Block plan.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Minor axis?
o: the shortest diameter of an ellipse, perpendicular to the major axis
the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the ground
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
items.s: Minor axis: the shortest diameter of an ellipse, perpendicular to the major axis. The other options describe Representative fraction, End elevation, Projection line.

items.q: Which term is described by “the line on a map or plan joining points of equal level”?
o: Longitudinal section
Cross section
Schedule of materials
Contour line
items.s: Contour line is the line on a map or plan joining points of equal level.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Leader line.
o: the actual length of an edge before it is shortened by projection
a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees
one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names
items.s: Leader line: the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names. The other options describe True length, Isometric projection, Principal view.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Lettering?
o: the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
the freehand standard style of characters used to annotate a drawing
a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched
items.s: Lettering: the freehand standard style of characters used to annotate a drawing. The other options describe Enlarging scale, Drawing sheet size, Sectional view.

items.q: Principal view may be defined as
o: a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base
items.s: Principal view: one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected. The other options describe Frustum, Projection line, French curve.

items.q: Which term is described by “the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total”?
o: Eccentricity
Hyperbola
Ellipse
Directrix
items.s: Ellipse is the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total.

items.q: The statement “the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles” describes which of the following?
o: Full size drawing
Reducing scale
Set square
French curve
items.s: Set square is the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles.

items.q: Which term is described by “the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job”?
o: Detail drawing
Site plan
Contour line
Schedule of materials
items.s: Schedule of materials is the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job.

items.q: Which term is described by “a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built”?
o: Spot level
Cross section
Detail drawing
Setting out
items.s: Detail drawing is a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built.

items.q: Which term is described by “the curve whose every point is equally distant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line”?
o: Normal
Parabola
Focus
Tangent
items.s: Parabola is the curve whose every point is equally distant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bar bending schedule.
o: the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed
the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
the table listing each reinforcement bar with its size, shape, length and number
items.s: Bar bending schedule: the table listing each reinforcement bar with its size, shape, length and number. The other options describe Working drawing, Inclination, Enlarging scale.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Tee square.
o: the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines
the distance from the apex of a cone to a point on the rim of its base
the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
items.s: Tee square: the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines. The other options describe Slant height, Inclination, Block plan.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hidden detail line?
o: the reduced scale used on isometric drawings so that projected lengths match the true view
the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane
the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job
the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view
items.s: Hidden detail line: the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view. The other options describe Isometric scale, Schedule of materials, True shape of section.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Principal view?
o: one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Arrowhead means.
