the placing of all dimensions from one common reference on the drawing
the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines
the pointed end of a dimension line, drawn about three times as long as it is wide
items.s: Arrowhead: the pointed end of a dimension line, drawn about three times as long as it is wide. The other options describe Note, Baseline dimensioning, Aligned dimensioning.

items.q: Which term is described by “one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected”?
o: Third angle projection
Principal view
End elevation
Projection line
items.s: Principal view is one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Setting out means.
o: the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground
a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
items.s: Setting out: the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground. The other options describe Longitudinal section, Block plan, Detail drawing.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names”
o: Centre line
Line weight
Leader line
Hidden detail line
items.s: Leader line is the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature”
o: Dimension line
Hatching line
Centre line
Break line
items.s: Centre line is the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature.

items.q: In this course, Isometric projection refers to
o: a pictorial view in which the front face is drawn true and the depth is drawn at an angle
any drawing that shows an object as it appears in three dimensions
an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale
a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees
items.s: Isometric projection: a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees. The other options describe Pictorial drawing, Oblique projection, Cavalier projection.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Longitudinal section means.
o: the drawing that shows the position of works within the site boundary at a small scale
the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed
a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
items.s: Longitudinal section: a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length. The other options describe Working drawing, Site plan, Detail drawing.

items.q: In this course, Focus refers to
o: the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve
the curve whose every point is equally distant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
items.s: Focus: one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve. The other options describe Parabola, Normal, Eccentricity.

items.q: The best definition of Block plan among these is
o: the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed
a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
the table listing each reinforcement bar with its size, shape, length and number
the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
items.s: Block plan: the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval. The other options describe Bar bending schedule, Working drawing, Longitudinal section.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Frustum means.
o: the curved or side surface of a solid between its two ends
the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base
items.s: Frustum: the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base. The other options describe Inclination, Lateral surface, Development.

items.q: Hidden detail line is best described as
o: the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind
the heavy line with arrows that shows where a section is taken
the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view
the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
items.s: Hidden detail line: the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view. The other options describe Cutting plane line, Extension line, Line weight.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the thin line between two arrowheads that carries the value of a measurement”
o: Hidden detail line
Leader line
Extension line
Dimension line
items.s: Dimension line is the thin line between two arrowheads that carries the value of a measurement.

items.q: The statement “the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth” describes which of the following?
o: Orthographic projection
Front elevation
Plan
End elevation
items.s: End elevation is the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Auxiliary view means.
o: the actual length of an edge before it is shortened by projection
a view projected on a plane not parallel to a principal plane, used to show a sloping face truly
the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
items.s: Auxiliary view: a view projected on a plane not parallel to a principal plane, used to show a sloping face truly. The other options describe Inclination, Development, True length.

items.q: In this course, Enlarging scale refers to
o: the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet
the panel of a drawing sheet that records the project, drawing number, scale and date
a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
items.s: Enlarging scale: a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents. The other options describe Border line, Drawing sheet size, Title block.

items.q: The statement “the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines” describes which of the following?
o: Baseline dimensioning
Aligned dimensioning
Arrowhead
Unidirectional dimensioning
items.s: Aligned dimensioning is the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Compass means.
o: a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
the instrument with two legs used to strike circles and arcs
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the ground
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
items.s: Compass: the instrument with two legs used to strike circles and arcs. The other options describe Drawing sheet size, French curve, Representative fraction.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to True lengths and developments?
o: True length
Auxiliary view
Inclination
Focus
items.s: Every other option belongs to True lengths and developments. “Focus” belongs to Conic sections, not True lengths and developments.

items.q: The best definition of Front elevation among these is
o: the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth
the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight
items.s: Front elevation: the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight. The other options describe End elevation, Projection line, Orthographic projection.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight”
o: Principal plane
Projection line
Front elevation
Third angle projection
items.s: Front elevation is the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight.

items.q: Orthographic projection is best described as
o: the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles
the arrangement in which the plane lies between observer and object, so views land on the near side
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
items.s: Orthographic projection: the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles. The other options describe Third angle projection, Projection line, First angle projection.

items.q: The best definition of Representative fraction among these is
o: a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the ground
the panel of a drawing sheet that records the project, drawing number, scale and date
items.s: Representative fraction: the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the ground. The other options describe Title block, Enlarging scale, French curve.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Principal view means.
o: the arrangement in which the plane lies between observer and object, so views land on the near side
one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work
items.s: Principal view: one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected. The other options describe Plan, Third angle projection, First angle projection.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Orthographic projection means.
o: the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles
the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth
items.s: Orthographic projection: the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles. The other options describe Plan, End elevation, Projection line.

items.q: The best definition of Aligned dimensioning among these is
o: the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines
the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom
the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row
the placing of all dimensions from one common reference on the drawing
items.s: Aligned dimensioning: the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines. The other options describe Chain dimensioning, Baseline dimensioning, Unidirectional dimensioning.

items.q: French curve is best described as
o: a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object
the instrument with two legs used to strike circles and arcs
the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet
items.s: French curve: a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves. The other options describe Scale, Compass, Border line.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Detail drawing means.
o: the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed
the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
items.s: Detail drawing: a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built. The other options describe Working drawing, Schedule of materials, Longitudinal section.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Projection line means.
o: the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
the view seen from the side of the object, showing height and depth
one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
items.s: Projection line: the faint line joining corresponding features in related views. The other options describe Principal view, End elevation, First angle projection.

items.q: Spot level is best described as
o: a drawing showing the cut profile of a road, drain or embankment across its width
the table listing each reinforcement bar with its size, shape, length and number
a written level at a stated point on a plan
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
items.s: Spot level: a written level at a stated point on a plan. The other options describe Bar bending schedule, Cross section, Detail drawing.

items.q: Projection line is best described as
o: the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
the arrangement in which the plane lies between observer and object, so views land on the near side
the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work
items.s: Projection line: the faint line joining corresponding features in related views. The other options describe Plan, Third angle projection, First angle projection.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the pointed end of a dimension line, drawn about three times as long as it is wide”
o: Note
Unidirectional dimensioning
Dimensioning
Arrowhead
items.s: Arrowhead is the pointed end of a dimension line, drawn about three times as long as it is wide.

items.q: Which term is described by “the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it”?
o: Focus
Tangent
Ellipse
Directrix
items.s: Tangent is the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it.

items.q: Focus is best described as
o: one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve
the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total
the fixed straight line from which distances define a conic curve
items.s: Focus: one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve. The other options describe Ellipse, Directrix, Eccentricity.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Tangent means.
o: the longest diameter of an ellipse, passing through both foci
the curve whose every point is equally distant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line
the fixed straight line from which distances define a conic curve
the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
items.s: Tangent: the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it. The other options describe Major axis, Parabola, Directrix.

items.q: A straight line rises 2000 mm over a horizontal distance of 6000 mm. Find its angle of inclination to the horizontal in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(2000/6000) = 18.43 degrees.

items.q: A cone of base radius 40 mm has a slant height of 120 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 40/120 = 120 degrees.

items.q: Calculate each interior angle of a regular polygon of 10 sides, in degrees.
items.s: Each interior angle = (n - 2) x 180/n = (10 - 2) x 180/10 = 144 degrees.

items.q: A line 75 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:50. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 75 x 50 = 3750 mm = 3.75 m.

items.q: A detail drawn at 1:50 appears again on a layout at 1:1000. By what factor is the layout drawing smaller than the detail?
items.s: The same real length is drawn 1000/50 times smaller, so the factor is 1000/50 = 20.

items.q: A drawing sheet measures 594 mm by 210 mm. Find the length of its diagonal in mm.
items.s: Diagonal = sqrt(594^2 + 210^2) = 630 mm.

items.q: Find the area of the lateral surface development of a cylinder of diameter 300 mm and height 500 mm, in mm2.
items.s: Area = pi d h = pi x 300 x 500 = 471239 mm2.

items.q: A cone has base radius 80 mm and vertical height 240 mm. Find its slant height in mm.
items.s: Slant height = sqrt(80^2 + 240^2) = 253 mm.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 180 mm and sector angle 100.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.2778 x 2 x pi x 180 = 314.2 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2.

items.q: A rectangular box 800 mm by 500 mm by 500 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(800 + 500) = 2600 mm; area = 2600 x 500 = 1300000 mm2.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 42 degrees and 47 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 42 - 47 = 91 degrees.

items.q: A development sector has radius 100 mm and angle 90 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A rectangular beam 250 mm wide and 200 mm deep is cut across. Find the area of the hatched section face in mm2.
items.s: Section area = 250 x 200 = 50000 mm2.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 120 mm, top radius 100 mm and vertical height 240 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A face 4000 mm long is inclined at 60 degrees to the plane of projection. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: Fore-shortened length = true x cos(angle), so true = 4000/cos(60) = 8000 mm.

items.q: A cone of base radius 60 mm has a slant height of 120 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 60/120 = 180 degrees.

items.q: A line 90 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:100. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 90 x 100 = 9000 mm = 9 m.

items.q: A drawing sheet measures 594 mm by 297 mm. Find the length of its diagonal in mm.
items.s: Diagonal = sqrt(594^2 + 297^2) = 664.1 mm.

items.q: A pipeline runs 5000 mm in plan and rises 3000 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(5000^2 + 3000^2) = 5831 mm.

items.q: Find the area of the lateral surface development of a cylinder of diameter 200 mm and height 300 mm, in mm2.
items.s: Area = pi d h = pi x 200 x 300 = 188496 mm2.

items.q: A rectangular box 600 mm by 700 mm by 500 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(600 + 700) = 2600 mm; area = 2600 x 500 = 1300000 mm2.

items.q: Find the eccentricity of an ellipse whose semi axes are 75 mm and 40 mm.
A drawing triangle shows two angles of 35 degrees and 58 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 35 - 58 = 87 degrees.

items.q: A hatched section is 180 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 10 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 180/10 + 1 = 18 + 1 = 19.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 120 mm, top radius 60 mm and vertical height 240 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A distance of 100 mm on paper represents 10.0 m on site. Find the scale of the drawing as 1:n, giving n.
items.s: n = real mm / drawn mm = 10000.0/100 = 100.

items.q: A cone of base radius 40 mm has a slant height of 150 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 40/150 = 96 degrees.

items.q: A wall 24.0 m long is drawn at a scale of 1:200. Calculate its length on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Length on paper = actual in mm / scale = 24000.0/200 = 120 mm.

items.q: A line 60 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:200. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 60 x 200 = 12000 mm = 12 m.

items.q: A pipeline runs 3000 mm in plan and rises 2000 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(3000^2 + 2000^2) = 3606 mm.

items.q: A cylinder of diameter 400 mm is developed. Find the length of the development in mm.
items.s: Development length = pi d = pi x 400 = 1257 mm.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 150 mm and sector angle 144.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.4 x 2 x pi x 150 = 377 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2.

items.q: A rectangular box 600 mm by 400 mm by 400 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(600 + 400) = 2000 mm; area = 2000 x 400 = 800000 mm2.

items.q: A plot of area 120.0 m2 is drawn at 1:50. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 120.0 m2 = 120000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 120000000.0/50^2 = 48000 mm2.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 35 degrees and 72 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 35 - 72 = 73 degrees.

items.q: A development sector has radius 120 mm and angle 180 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A hatched section is 200 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 5 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 200/5 + 1 = 40 + 1 = 41.

items.q: A rectangular beam 300 mm wide and 150 mm deep is cut across. Find the area of the hatched section face in mm2.
items.s: Section area = 300 x 150 = 45000 mm2.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 150 mm, top radius 100 mm and vertical height 150 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A cube of edge 60 mm is drawn in isometric. Find the length used for each edge on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Each edge is drawn at 0.816 x true = 0.816 x 60 = 48.96 mm.

items.q: A distance of 50 mm on paper represents 8.0 m on site. Find the scale of the drawing as 1:n, giving n.
items.s: n = real mm / drawn mm = 8000.0/50 = 160.

items.q: A line measures 82 mm on an isometric drawing. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: True length = isometric/0.816 = 82/0.816 = 100.5 mm.

items.q: A cone of base radius 90 mm has a slant height of 200 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 90/200 = 162 degrees.

items.q: A detail drawn at 1:50 appears again on a layout at 1:200. By what factor is the layout drawing smaller than the detail?
items.s: The same real length is drawn 200/50 times smaller, so the factor is 200/50 = 4.

items.q: A pipeline runs 5000 mm in plan and rises 2500 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(5000^2 + 2500^2) = 5590 mm.

items.q: A rectangular box 600 mm by 400 mm by 300 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(600 + 400) = 2000 mm; area = 2000 x 300 = 600000 mm2.

items.q: Find the eccentricity of an ellipse whose semi axes are 60 mm and 60 mm.
items.s: c = sqrt(60^2 - 60^2) = 0.0; eccentricity = c/a = 0.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 35 degrees and 47 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 35 - 47 = 98 degrees.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 180 mm, top radius 60 mm and vertical height 150 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A distance of 80 mm on paper represents 8.0 m on site. Find the scale of the drawing as 1:n, giving n.
items.s: n = real mm / drawn mm = 8000.0/80 = 100.

items.q: A cone of base radius 90 mm has a slant height of 120 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 90/120 = 270 degrees.

items.q: Calculate each interior angle of a regular polygon of 5 sides, in degrees.
items.s: Each interior angle = (n - 2) x 180/n = (5 - 2) x 180/5 = 108 degrees.

items.q: A line 90 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:50. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 90 x 50 = 4500 mm = 4.5 m.

items.q: A detail drawn at 1:200 appears again on a layout at 1:200. By what factor is the layout drawing smaller than the detail?
items.s: The same real length is drawn 200/200 times smaller, so the factor is 200/200 = 1.

items.q: An edge of true length 120 mm is to be drawn in isometric. Using the isometric scale, find its drawn length in mm.
items.s: Isometric length = 0.816 x true = 0.816 x 120 = 97.92 mm.

items.q: A pipeline runs 3000 mm in plan and rises 2500 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(3000^2 + 2500^2) = 3905 mm.

items.q: Find the area of the lateral surface development of a cylinder of diameter 300 mm and height 250 mm, in mm2.
items.s: Area = pi d h = pi x 300 x 250 = 235619 mm2.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 200 mm and sector angle 108.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.3 x 2 x pi x 200 = 377 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2.

items.q: A rectangular box 800 mm by 500 mm by 400 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(800 + 500) = 2600 mm; area = 2600 x 400 = 1040000 mm2.

items.q: A plot of area 96.0 m2 is drawn at 1:50. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 96.0 m2 = 96000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 96000000.0/50^2 = 38400 mm2.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Eccentricity.
o: the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
items.s: Eccentricity: the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola. The other options describe Ellipse, Normal, Tangent.

items.q: Which term is described by “the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature”?
o: Cutting plane line
Dimension line
Line weight
Centre line
items.s: Centre line is the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature.

items.q: Tee square may be defined as
o: the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object
items.s: Tee square: the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines. The other options describe Scale, Enlarging scale, Drawing sheet size.

items.q: Section plane may be defined as
o: the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched
a view in which one quarter of the object is removed so both inside and outside are seen
the imaginary plane along which an object is cut for a sectional view
the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane
items.s: Section plane: the imaginary plane along which an object is cut for a sectional view. The other options describe Sectional view, Half section, True shape of section.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Orthographic projection?
o: First angle projection
True length
Third angle projection
Orthographic projection
items.s: Every other option belongs to Orthographic projection. “True length” belongs to True lengths and developments, not Orthographic projection.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cavalier projection?
o: an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale
a line drawn parallel to one of the three isometric axes
the reduced scale used on isometric drawings so that projected lengths match the true view
an oblique view in which the depth is drawn at half its true scale
items.s: Cavalier projection: an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale. The other options describe Isometric line, Cabinet projection, Isometric scale.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Longitudinal section.
o: the drawing that shows the position of works within the site boundary at a small scale
a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground
a written level at a stated point on a plan
items.s: Longitudinal section: a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length. The other options describe Setting out, Spot level, Site plan.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Schedule of materials.
o: the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job
the drawing that shows the position of works within the site boundary at a small scale
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
a drawing showing the cut profile of a road, drain or embankment across its width
items.s: Schedule of materials: the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job. The other options describe Detail drawing, Cross section, Site plan.

items.q: Hidden detail line may be defined as
o: the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names
the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view
the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind
the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
items.s: Hidden detail line: the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view. The other options describe Leader line, Extension line, Line weight.

items.q: Sectional view may be defined as
o: the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched
a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself
the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation
the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane
items.s: Sectional view: the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched. The other options describe True shape of section, Revolved section, Mean line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Isometric projection?
o: an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale
the reduced scale used on isometric drawings so that projected lengths match the true view
a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees
an oblique view in which the depth is drawn at half its true scale
items.s: Isometric projection: a pictorial view in which the three axes are set at equal angles of one hundred and twenty degrees. The other options describe Cabinet projection, Cavalier projection, Isometric scale.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the line on a map or plan joining points of equal level”
o: Contour line
Site plan
Working drawing
Setting out
items.s: Contour line is the line on a map or plan joining points of equal level.

items.q: Which term is described by “the drawing that shows the position of works within the site boundary at a small scale”?
o: Bar bending schedule
Contour line
Setting out
Site plan
items.s: Site plan is the drawing that shows the position of works within the site boundary at a small scale.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles”?
o: Plan
Principal plane
First angle projection
Orthographic projection
items.s: Orthographic projection is the method of showing an object by separate views projected onto planes at right angles.

items.q: Leader line may be defined as
o: the thin evenly spaced line drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a section
the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names
the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view
the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
items.s: Leader line: the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names. The other options describe Hatching line, Extension line, Hidden detail line.

items.q: Setting out may be defined as
o: a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground
the drawing that shows the position of works within the site boundary at a small scale
a drawing showing the cut profile of a road, drain or embankment across its width
items.s: Setting out: the transfer of the lines of a planned structure from the drawing onto the ground. The other options describe Detail drawing, Cross section, Site plan.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Frustum?
o: the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base
the distance from the apex of a cone to a point on the rim of its base
a view projected on a plane not parallel to a principal plane, used to show a sloping face truly
the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
items.s: Frustum: the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base. The other options describe Slant height, Development, Auxiliary view.

items.q: Focus may be defined as
o: the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
the curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed points always add to the same total
one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
items.s: Focus: one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve. The other options describe Ellipse, Tangent, Normal.

items.q: Dimensioning may be defined as
o: the placing of all dimensions from one common reference on the drawing
the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row
the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made
the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines
items.s: Dimensioning: the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made. The other options describe Chain dimensioning, Baseline dimensioning, Aligned dimensioning.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles”
o: Compass
Set square
Title block
Representative fraction
items.s: Set square is the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles.

items.q: Lettering is best described as
o: the placing of all dimensions from one common reference on the drawing
the written instruction on a drawing that a dimension cannot express
the freehand standard style of characters used to annotate a drawing
the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made
items.s: Lettering: the freehand standard style of characters used to annotate a drawing. The other options describe Note, Baseline dimensioning, Dimensioning.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a view projected on a plane not parallel to a principal plane, used to show a sloping face truly”
o: Inclination
True length
Auxiliary view
Development
items.s: Auxiliary view is a view projected on a plane not parallel to a principal plane, used to show a sloping face truly.

items.q: Which term is described by “the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded”?
o: Inclination
Development
Auxiliary view
Slant height
items.s: Development is the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded.

items.q: Principal plane is best described as
o: the faint line joining corresponding features in related views
the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected
the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work
the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
items.s: Principal plane: the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected. The other options describe First angle projection, Plan, Projection line.

items.q: Which term is described by “any drawing that shows an object as it appears in three dimensions”?
o: Isometric scale
Isometric projection
Pictorial drawing
Oblique projection
items.s: Pictorial drawing is any drawing that shows an object as it appears in three dimensions.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work”
o: Front elevation
Plan
First angle projection
Principal view
items.s: Plan is the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Line weight.
o: the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view
the line that shows a part of a long object has been left out to save space
the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind
the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names
items.s: Line weight: the thickness of a drawn line, chosen to show the relative importance of each kind. The other options describe Leader line, Break line, Hidden detail line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Isometric scale?
o: any drawing that shows an object as it appears in three dimensions
a pictorial view in which the front face is drawn true and the depth is drawn at an angle
the reduced scale used on isometric drawings so that projected lengths match the true view
an oblique view in which the full depth of the object is drawn to scale
items.s: Isometric scale: the reduced scale used on isometric drawings so that projected lengths match the true view. The other options describe Cavalier projection, Pictorial drawing, Oblique projection.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet”
o: Reducing scale
Set square
Border line
French curve
items.s: Border line is the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet.

items.q: Scale may be defined as
o: the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the ground
the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object
the instrument with two legs used to strike circles and arcs
items.s: Scale: the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object. The other options describe Set square, Representative fraction, Compass.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Conic sections?
o: Title block
Hyperbola
Parabola
Ellipse
items.s: Every other option belongs to Conic sections. “Title block” belongs to Drawing instruments and standards, not Conic sections.

items.q: Extension line is best described as
o: the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
the line that shows a part of a long object has been left out to save space
the thin line between two arrowheads that carries the value of a measurement
the thin evenly spaced line drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a section
items.s: Extension line: the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line. The other options describe Hatching line, Break line, Dimension line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Principal plane?
o: the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected
one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
the view of an object seen from the front at right angles to the direction of sight
items.s: Principal plane: the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected. The other options describe Front elevation, First angle projection, Principal view.

items.q: Title block may be defined as
o: the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles
a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
the panel of a drawing sheet that records the project, drawing number, scale and date
items.s: Title block: the panel of a drawing sheet that records the project, drawing number, scale and date. The other options describe Drawing sheet size, French curve, Set square.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Detail drawing?
o: a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job
a written level at a stated point on a plan
items.s: Detail drawing: a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built. The other options describe Schedule of materials, Spot level, Longitudinal section.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Leader line?
o: the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature
the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names
the heavy line with arrows that shows where a section is taken
items.s: Leader line: the thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note to the feature it names. The other options describe Extension line, Centre line, Cutting plane line.

items.q: Working drawing may be defined as
o: the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed
a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
a drawing showing the cut profile of a road, drain or embankment across its width
items.s: Working drawing: the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed. The other options describe Longitudinal section, Detail drawing, Cross section.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a line drawn parallel to one of the three isometric axes”
o: Pictorial drawing
Oblique projection
Isometric line
Cavalier projection
items.s: Isometric line is a line drawn parallel to one of the three isometric axes.

items.q: Which term is described by “the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched”?
o: Sectional view
Section plane
Mean line
True shape of section
items.s: Sectional view is the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Frustum.
o: the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
the distance from the apex of a cone to a point on the rim of its base
the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base
the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
items.s: Frustum: the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base. The other options describe Development, Inclination, Slant height.

items.q: Baseline dimensioning may be defined as
o: the freehand standard style of characters used to annotate a drawing
the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom
the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made
the placing of all dimensions from one common reference on the drawing
items.s: Baseline dimensioning: the placing of all dimensions from one common reference on the drawing. The other options describe Lettering, Dimensioning, Unidirectional dimensioning.

items.q: Drawing sheet size is best described as
o: the panel of a drawing sheet that records the project, drawing number, scale and date
the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
a drawing made at the actual size of the object
items.s: Drawing sheet size: the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared. The other options describe Title block, Tee square, Full size drawing.

items.q: Parabola is best described as
o: the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
the curve whose every point is equally distant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line
items.s: Parabola: the curve whose every point is equally distant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line. The other options describe Tangent, Focus, Normal.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Tangent?
o: the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
the fixed straight line from which distances define a conic curve
the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
items.s: Tangent: the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it. The other options describe Directrix, Eccentricity, Normal.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Focus?
o: the fixed straight line from which distances define a conic curve
the ratio that fixes the shape of a conic curve, below one for an ellipse and one for a parabola
one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve
the line drawn perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact
items.s: Focus: one of the fixed points used in defining a conic curve. The other options describe Normal, Eccentricity, Directrix.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval”
o: Schedule of materials
Spot level
Bar bending schedule
Block plan
items.s: Block plan is the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Inclination?
o: the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base
the curved or side surface of a solid between its two ends
the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
items.s: Inclination: the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane. The other options describe Frustum, Lateral surface, Development.

items.q: Aligned dimensioning may be defined as
o: the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row
the written instruction on a drawing that a dimension cannot express
the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines
the freehand standard style of characters used to annotate a drawing
items.s: Aligned dimensioning: the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines. The other options describe Chain dimensioning, Lettering, Note.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed”
o: Setting out
Schedule of materials
Block plan
Working drawing
items.s: Working drawing is the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it”
o: Major axis
Tangent
Normal
Minor axis
items.s: Tangent is the straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the written instruction on a drawing that a dimension cannot express”
o: Lettering
Arrowhead
Note
Chain dimensioning
items.s: Note is the written instruction on a drawing that a dimension cannot express.

items.q: Which term is described by “the curved or side surface of a solid between its two ends”?
o: Lateral surface
Slant height
Inclination
Frustum
items.s: Lateral surface is the curved or side surface of a solid between its two ends.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Unidirectional dimensioning?
o: the system in which dimension figures are written parallel to their dimension lines
the placing of dimensions end to end in a continuous row
the placing of sizes and notes on a drawing so that the object can be made
the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom
items.s: Unidirectional dimensioning: the system in which all dimension figures are written horizontal and read from the bottom. The other options describe Chain dimensioning, Dimensioning, Aligned dimensioning.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Spot level.
o: a written level at a stated point on a plan
the line on a map or plan joining points of equal level
the fully dimensioned drawing from which a structure is actually constructed
a large scale drawing of one part of a structure showing how it is built
items.s: Spot level: a written level at a stated point on a plan. The other options describe Detail drawing, Working drawing, Contour line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Schedule of materials?
o: a drawing showing the profile of a route or drain along its length
the line on a map or plan joining points of equal level
the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job
the outline plan of proposed buildings on a site, used for planning approval
items.s: Schedule of materials: the tabulated list of the quantities and specifications of the materials in a job. The other options describe Contour line, Longitudinal section, Block plan.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Border line?
o: a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
a drawing made at the actual size of the object
the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet
a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
items.s: Border line: the heavy frame drawn round the drawing area of a sheet. The other options describe Full size drawing, Enlarging scale, French curve.

items.q: Full size drawing may be defined as
o: a drawing made at the actual size of the object
the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles
the standard trimmed dimension of a sheet on which a drawing is prepared
a scale in which the drawing is smaller than the object it represents
items.s: Full size drawing: a drawing made at the actual size of the object. The other options describe Drawing sheet size, Reducing scale, Set square.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Reducing scale.
o: the triangular instrument used with a tee square to draw lines at fixed angles
the fixed relationship between drawn size and real size of an object
a scale in which the drawing is smaller than the object it represents
the instrument whose stock rides the board edge to guide horizontal lines
items.s: Reducing scale: a scale in which the drawing is smaller than the object it represents. The other options describe Set square, Scale, Tee square.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines First angle projection?
o: one of the six standard directions from which an object is projected
the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side
the view of an object seen from above, drawn below the elevation in first angle work
the reference plane against which elevations, plans and side views are projected
items.s: First angle projection: the arrangement in which an object is placed between the observer and the plane, so views land on the far side. The other options describe Plan, Principal view, Principal plane.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Revolved section?
o: the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation
the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched
a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself
the exact outline of a cut surface, found by projecting it onto a plane parallel to the cutting plane
items.s: Revolved section: a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself. The other options describe Mean line, True shape of section, Sectional view.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Extension line.
o: the line that shows a part of a long object has been left out to save space
the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line
the thin line between two arrowheads that carries the value of a measurement
the heavy line with arrows that shows where a section is taken
items.s: Extension line: the thin line drawn from the feature to meet a dimension line. The other options describe Cutting plane line, Dimension line, Break line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Development?
o: the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded
the angle a line or surface makes with a stated reference plane
the curved or side surface of a solid between its two ends
the lower part of a solid left when its top is cut off parallel to the base
items.s: Development: the flat pattern obtained when the surface of a solid is unfolded. The other options describe Lateral surface, Inclination, Frustum.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hatching line?
o: the chain line of long and short dashes that marks the axis of a symmetrical feature
the short dashed line that shows an edge which is not visible in the view
the thin evenly spaced line drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a section
the heavy line with arrows that shows where a section is taken
items.s: Hatching line: the thin evenly spaced line drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a section. The other options describe Centre line, Hidden detail line, Cutting plane line.

items.q: Mean line is best described as
o: the view obtained by imagining the object cut open and the cut face hatched
a small section turned through ninety degrees and drawn on the view itself
the imaginary plane along which an object is cut for a sectional view
the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation
items.s: Mean line: the thin centre line drawn through a rivet, bolt or other repeated feature in elevation. The other options describe Revolved section, Sectional view, Section plane.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Enlarging scale.
o: a scale in which the drawing is smaller than the object it represents
a template with a variable curve used to draw smooth non circular curves
a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the ground
items.s: Enlarging scale: a scale in which the drawing is larger than the object it represents. The other options describe Representative fraction, French curve, Reducing scale.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 200 mm and sector angle 144.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.4 x 2 x pi x 200 = 502.7 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2 = 502.6.

items.q: A rectangular box 1000 mm by 500 mm by 300 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(1000 + 500) = 3000 mm; area = 3000 x 300 = 900000 mm2.

items.q: A plot of area 200.0 m2 is drawn at 1:100. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 200.0 m2 = 200000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 200000000.0/100^2 = 20000 mm2.

items.q: A wall 24.0 m long is drawn at a scale of 1:50. Calculate its length on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Length on paper = actual in mm / scale = 24000.0/50 = 480 mm.

items.q: A pipeline runs 4000 mm in plan and rises 3000 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(4000^2 + 3000^2) = 5000 mm.

items.q: A straight line rises 1500 mm over a horizontal distance of 5000 mm. Find its angle of inclination to the horizontal in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(1500/5000) = 16.7 degrees.

items.q: A cone of base radius 60 mm has a slant height of 200 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 60/200 = 108 degrees.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 55 degrees and 47 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 55 - 47 = 78 degrees.

items.q: A rectangular beam 300 mm wide and 200 mm deep is cut across. Find the area of the hatched section face in mm2.
items.s: Section area = 300 x 200 = 60000 mm2.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 120 mm, top radius 100 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A detail drawn at 1:200 appears again on a layout at 1:1000. By what factor is the layout drawing smaller than the detail?
items.s: The same real length is drawn 1000/200 times smaller, so the factor is 1000/200 = 5.

items.q: Two lines forming a right triangle have lengths 3000 mm and 5000 mm at the right angle. Find the angle opposite the 5000 mm side, in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(5000/3000) = 59.04 degrees.

items.q: A plot of area 200.0 m2 is drawn at 1:50. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 200.0 m2 = 200000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 200000000.0/50^2 = 80000 mm2.

items.q: A development sector has radius 80 mm and angle 90 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A cone has base radius 80 mm and vertical height 150 mm. Find its slant height in mm.
items.s: Slant height = sqrt(80^2 + 150^2) = 170 mm.

items.q: An ellipse has semi major axis 90 mm and semi minor axis 60 mm. Find the distance from the centre to each focus in mm.
items.s: Focal distance = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(90^2 - 60^2) = 67.08 mm.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 68 degrees and 47 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 68 - 47 = 65 degrees.

items.q: A rectangular box 600 mm by 700 mm by 400 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(600 + 700) = 2600 mm; area = 2600 x 400 = 1040000 mm2.

items.q: A development sector has radius 120 mm and angle 135 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A wall 12.0 m long is drawn at a scale of 1:200. Calculate its length on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Length on paper = actual in mm / scale = 12000.0/200 = 60 mm.

items.q: A pipeline runs 5000 mm in plan and rises 2000 mm in the same length. Find the true length of the pipe in mm.
items.s: True length = sqrt(5000^2 + 2000^2) = 5385 mm.

items.q: A face 3000 mm long is inclined at 60 degrees to the plane of projection. Find its true length in mm.
items.s: Fore-shortened length = true x cos(angle), so true = 3000/cos(60) = 6000 mm.

items.q: A cone of base radius 60 mm has a slant height of 250 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 60/250 = 86.4 degrees.

items.q: An ellipse has semi major axis 75 mm and semi minor axis 50 mm. Find the distance from the centre to each focus in mm.
items.s: Focal distance = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(75^2 - 50^2) = 55.9 mm.

items.q: A wall 12.0 m long is drawn at a scale of 1:100. Calculate its length on the drawing in mm.
items.s: Length on paper = actual in mm / scale = 12000.0/100 = 120 mm.

items.q: A cone of base radius 75 mm has a slant height of 120 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 75/120 = 225 degrees.

items.q: A hatched section is 200 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 8 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 200/8 + 1 = 25 + 1 = 26.

items.q: A rectangular beam 200 mm wide and 150 mm deep is cut across. Find the area of the hatched section face in mm2.
items.s: Section area = 200 x 150 = 30000 mm2.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 120 mm, top radius 80 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
Two lines forming a right triangle have lengths 4000 mm and 6000 mm at the right angle. Find the angle opposite the 6000 mm side, in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(6000/4000) = 56.31 degrees.

items.q: The development of a cone has radius 180 mm and sector angle 160.0 degrees. Find the arc length of the sector in mm.
items.s: Arc = (angle/360) x 2 pi R = 0.4444 x 2 x pi x 180 = 502.7 mm, which equals pi x base radius x 2 = 502.6.

items.q: A rectangular box 1000 mm by 700 mm by 500 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(1000 + 700) = 3400 mm; area = 3400 x 500 = 1700000 mm2.

items.q: A line 120 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:200. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 120 x 200 = 24000 mm = 24 m.

items.q: A straight line rises 1500 mm over a horizontal distance of 4000 mm. Find its angle of inclination to the horizontal in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(1500/4000) = 20.56 degrees.

items.q: A cone has base radius 60 mm and vertical height 150 mm. Find its slant height in mm.
items.s: Slant height = sqrt(60^2 + 150^2) = 161.6 mm.

items.q: An ellipse has semi major axis 90 mm and semi minor axis 50 mm. Find the distance from the centre to each focus in mm.
items.s: Focal distance = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(90^2 - 50^2) = 74.83 mm.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 55 degrees and 72 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 55 - 72 = 53 degrees.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 150 mm, top radius 80 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A line 90 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:200. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 90 x 200 = 18000 mm = 18 m.

items.q: A cone of base radius 90 mm has a slant height of 150 mm. Find the angle of the development sector in degrees.
items.s: Sector angle = 360 x r/L = 360 x 90/150 = 216 degrees.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 180 mm, top radius 60 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A rectangular box 800 mm by 700 mm by 300 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(800 + 700) = 3000 mm; area = 3000 x 300 = 900000 mm2.

items.q: A plot of area 120.0 m2 is drawn at 1:100. Find the area of the plot on the drawing in mm2.
items.s: Areas scale as the square of the scale: 120.0 m2 = 120000000.0 mm2, so drawn area = 120000000.0/100^2 = 12000 mm2.

items.q: A development sector has radius 100 mm and angle 120 degrees. Calculate its area in mm2.
A drawing sheet measures 594 mm by 420 mm. Find the length of its diagonal in mm.
items.s: Diagonal = sqrt(594^2 + 420^2) = 727.5 mm.

items.q: A cone has base radius 100 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find its slant height in mm.
items.s: Slant height = sqrt(100^2 + 200^2) = 223.6 mm.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 42 degrees and 72 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 42 - 72 = 66 degrees.

items.q: A hatched section is 180 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 6 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 180/6 + 1 = 30 + 1 = 31.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 150 mm, top radius 80 mm and vertical height 240 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A line 75 mm long on a drawing represents a length at scale 1:100. Find the real length in m.
items.s: Real length = 75 x 100 = 7500 mm = 7.5 m.

items.q: Find the eccentricity of an ellipse whose semi axes are 90 mm and 50 mm.
A hatched section is 120 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 5 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 120/5 + 1 = 24 + 1 = 25.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 120 mm, top radius 80 mm and vertical height 150 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
Two lines forming a right triangle have lengths 3000 mm and 6000 mm at the right angle. Find the angle opposite the 6000 mm side, in degrees.
items.s: Angle = tan-1(6000/3000) = 63.43 degrees.

items.q: A drawing sheet measures 420 mm by 210 mm. Find the length of its diagonal in mm.
items.s: Diagonal = sqrt(420^2 + 210^2) = 469.6 mm.

items.q: A drawing triangle shows two angles of 68 degrees and 58 degrees. Find the third angle in degrees.
items.s: Angles of a triangle total 180, so the third = 180 - 68 - 58 = 54 degrees.

items.q: A hatched section is 120 mm wide and hatching lines are spaced 10 mm apart, with a line at each edge. How many hatch lines are needed?
items.s: Number of lines = 120/10 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13.

items.q: A frustum has base radius 150 mm, top radius 60 mm and vertical height 200 mm. Find the slant height of its development in mm.
A rectangular box 600 mm by 500 mm by 300 mm high is developed. Find the area of its four vertical faces in mm2.
items.s: Perimeter of base = 2(600 + 500) = 2200 mm; area = 2200 x 300 = 660000 mm2.
